INTERMEDIATE1. Why Utility Types Exist

Definition

Utility types are built-in generic type transformations, shipped with TypeScript itself, that let you derive a new type from an existing one instead of hand-writing near-duplicate interfaces.

Real-world analogy: Utility types are like photo filters — you don't redraw the picture, you apply a transformation ("make everything optional", "keep only these fields") to a type you already have. 
interface User {
    id: number;
    name: string;
    email: string;
}

// Without utility types, you'd hand-write a near-duplicate:
interface UserUpdate {
    id?: number;
    name?: string;
    email?: string;
}

// With a utility type, derive it instead:
type UserUpdateBetter = Partial;

INTERMEDIATE2. Partial, Required, and Readonly

Partial<T> — Makes All Properties Optional

interface Task {
    id: number;
    title: string;
    done: boolean;
}

function updateTask(task: Task, changes: Partial): Task {
    return { ...task, ...changes };
}

updateTask({ id: 1, title: "Write", done: false }, { done: true });

Required<T> — Makes All Properties Mandatory

interface Config {
    host?: string;
    port?: number;
}

function connect(config: Required) {
    console.log(`${config.host}:${config.port}`);
}

connect({ host: "localhost", port: 8080 });   // ✅ both now required
// connect({ host: "localhost" });             // ❌ Error: 'port' is missing

Readonly<T> — Makes All Properties Immutable

interface Point { x: number; y: number; }

const frozen: Readonly = { x: 1, y: 2 };
// frozen.x = 5;   // ❌ Error: Cannot assign to 'x' because it is read-only

INTERMEDIATE3. Pick and Omit

Pick<T, Keys> — Select a Subset of Properties

interface User {
    id: number;
    name: string;
    email: string;
    passwordHash: string;
}

type PublicUser = Pick;
// { id: number; name: string; email: string }

const safeUser: PublicUser = { id: 1, name: "Kim", email: "kim@example.com" };

Omit<T, Keys> — Remove a Subset of Properties

type UserWithoutPassword = Omit;
// { id: number; name: string; email: string }

const publicProfile: UserWithoutPassword = {
    id: 1,
    name: "Kim",
    email: "kim@example.com"
};
💡 Tip: Pick and Omit are opposites of each other and are frequently used to shape DTOs (data transfer objects) from a larger domain model.

INTERMEDIATE4. Record

Record<Keys, Type> builds an object type whose keys are drawn from Keys and whose values are all of type Type — a type-safe dictionary.

type Role = "admin" | "editor" | "viewer";

const rolePermissions: Record = {
    admin: ["read", "write", "delete"],
    editor: ["read", "write"],
    viewer: ["read"]
};

// rolePermissions.superuser;   // ❌ Error: not a valid Role

type ErrorMessages = Record;
const messages: ErrorMessages = {
    required: "This field is required",
    invalid: "This value is invalid"
};

ADVANCED5. Extract, Exclude, and NonNullable

Extract<T, U> — Keep Only Matching Members

type Status = "pending" | "active" | "closed" | "archived";
type ActiveStatus = Extract;
// "pending" | "active"

Exclude<T, U> — Remove Matching Members

type InactiveStatus = Exclude;
// "closed" | "archived"

type EventType = "click" | "hover" | "scroll" | "keydown";
type MouseEvent2 = Exclude;
// "click" | "hover" | "scroll"

NonNullable<T> — Strip null and undefined

type MaybeString = string | null | undefined;
type DefiniteString = NonNullable;
// string

function process(value: NonNullable) {
    console.log(value.trim());   // safe - no null/undefined possible
}

ADVANCED6. Mapped Types

Mapped types let you build your own utility types by iterating over an existing type's keys with [K in keyof T].

type MyPartial = {
    [K in keyof T]?: T[K];
};

type MyReadonly = {
    readonly [K in keyof T]: T[K];
};

interface Task { id: number; title: string; }

type ReadonlyTask = MyReadonly;
// { readonly id: number; readonly title: string; }

Key Remapping with as

type Getters = {
    [K in keyof T as `get${Capitalize}`]: () => T[K];
};

interface Person { name: string; age: number; }

type PersonGetters = Getters;
// { getName: () => string; getAge: () => number; }

Removing Modifiers with - 

type Mutable = {
    -readonly [K in keyof T]: T[K];
};

type RequiredFields = {
    [K in keyof T]-?: T[K];
};

interface Frozen { readonly id?: number; }
type Unfrozen = Mutable>;
// { id: number; }

ADVANCED7. Conditional Types

Conditional types choose between two types based on a type-level check, using the familiar T extends U ? X : Y syntax.

type IsString = T extends string ? true : false;

type A = IsString<"hello">;   // true
type B = IsString<42>;        // false

Practical Conditional Type

type Flatten = T extends (infer Item)[] ? Item : T;

type A1 = Flatten;   // string
type A2 = Flatten;     // number (unchanged, not an array)

Distribution Over Unions (Recap)

type NonNull = T extends null | undefined ? never : T;

type Cleaned = NonNull;
// string | number  (never members are dropped from the resulting union)

ADVANCED8. infer in Conditional Types

The infer keyword captures a type from within a conditional check so you can reuse it in the result — it powers many of TypeScript's most useful built-in utilities.

// A simplified reimplementation of the built-in ReturnType
type MyReturnType = T extends (...args: any[]) => infer R ? R : never;

function getUser() {
    return { id: 1, name: "Val" };
}

type User = MyReturnType;
// { id: number; name: string; }

Extracting Array Element and Promise Types

type ElementType = T extends (infer E)[] ? E : never;
type Unwrapped = ElementType;   // string

type Awaited2 = T extends Promise ? V : T;
type ResolvedType = Awaited2>;   // number
💡 Tip: TypeScript ships a real Awaited<T> utility type (recursive, handling nested promises) used internally to type async/await — see the Async/Await with Types guide.

ADVANCED9. Template Literal Types

Template literal types build new string literal types by combining literal types the same way JavaScript template literals combine strings.

type Direction = "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right";
type Margin = `margin-${Direction}`;
// "margin-top" | "margin-bottom" | "margin-left" | "margin-right"

const style: Margin = "margin-top";
// const bad: Margin = "margin-center";   // ❌ Error

Combining Multiple Unions

type Size = "sm" | "md" | "lg";
type Color = "red" | "blue";

type ClassName = `btn-${Size}-${Color}`;
// "btn-sm-red" | "btn-sm-blue" | "btn-md-red" | "btn-md-blue" | "btn-lg-red" | "btn-lg-blue"

Real-World Use: Typed Event Names

type EntityName = "user" | "post" | "comment";
type EventName = `${EntityName}:${"created" | "updated" | "deleted"}`;
// "user:created" | "user:updated" | ... 9 total combinations

function on(event: EventName, handler: () => void) { /* ... */ }
on("user:created", () => console.log("A user was created"));
// on("user:renamed", () => {});   // ❌ Error: not a valid EventName

ADVANCED10. Best Practices

1. Reach for Built-in Utilities Before Writing Your Own

// ✅ Good - use what's already there
type UserUpdate = Partial>;
interface User { id: number; name: string; email: string; }

2. Name Complex Derived Types

// ✅ Good - reusable, self-documenting
type PublicUser = Omit;
interface User { passwordHash: string; }

3. Use Record for Dictionary-Shaped Data

// ✅ Good
const cache: Record = {};

4. Keep Conditional Types Readable

// ✅ Break deeply nested conditionals into named helper types
type IsArray = T extends unknown[] ? true : false;
type ArrayOrNever = IsArray extends true ? T : never;

5. Reserve infer for Genuine Type Extraction Needs

Most day-to-day code should use ReturnType<T>, Parameters<T>, and Awaited<T> rather than writing new infer-based types from scratch.

📋 Quick Reference Summary

Utility / Feature Key Points
Partial / Required / Readonly Toggle optionality and mutability across all properties
Pick / Omit Select or remove a specific subset of properties
Record<K, V> Type-safe dictionary keyed by a union or string type
Extract / Exclude Filter members in or out of a union type
NonNullable<T> Strips null and undefined from a type
Mapped types [K in keyof T] to build custom utility types, with as for key remapping
Conditional types T extends U ? X : Y, distributes over naked unions
infer Captures a type inside a conditional for reuse (powers ReturnType, Awaited)
Template literal types Combine string literal unions into new precise string types
